status_observed: 200 OK â€” response body shows "status": "SENT" for an invoice that was DRAFT, with "sent_at": null and "sent_by": null
what_is_wrong: Editing a DRAFT invoice silently promotes it to SENT without /send ever being called. The invoice is left in an inconsistent state (status SENT but sent_at/sent_by null), and because POST /invoices/{id}/send only accepts a DRAFT, that invoice can never afterwards be legitimately sent â€” /send returns 409 forever. So any draft that is edited even once loses its send step entirely (no sent_at audit trail, no customer notification). finance_engine.resolve_invoice_status_after_payment's own docstring states its floor is SENT and that it is "Only ever called after Sent (Draft->Sent is a separate, explicit action, never payment-derived)" â€” update_invoice calls it unconditionally, including on a DRAFT with zero payments.

suspected_cause: app/api/v1/invoices.py:566 â€” resolve_invoice_status_after_payment(...) is called in update_invoice with no guard for invoice.status == "DRAFT"; the function returns "SENT" as its floor when settled <= 0 (app/services/finance_engine.py:43-44)

what_is_wrong: Selecting a customer withholding tax head on an invoice payment computes nothing. The endpoint looks up the head, validates its scope/direction/date via validate_head_usable, snapshots its tax_name and print_label, and defaults withholding_calculated_on to SUBTOTAL â€” then never reads the head's rate_pct and never calls tax_engine. withheld_amount is taken verbatim from the client and defaults to 0, and withholding_calculated_on is persisted but never used to pick a basis. Net effect: a payment where the customer withheld tax at source under-settles the invoice, which keeps a phantom balance_due and leaves the invoice stuck at PART_PAID instead of PAID. The purchase-bill side of the very same feature does compute it (tax_engine.calculate_tax on a SUBTOTAL/TOTAL basis, with withholding_amount_override as an explicit override), so the two directions of the same withholding feature disagree.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/invoices.py:625 â€” `withheld_amount = body.withheld_amount or Decimal("0")`; the head loaded at line 634 is used only for name/label snapshots, and build_tax_head_snapshot/tax_engine.calculate_tax are never called on this path (compare app/api/v1/purchase_bills.py:247-251)

status_observed: 500 Internal Server Error â€” {"detail": "Internal server error"}
what_is_wrong: An out-of-enum `reason` value returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx. The OpenAPI schema types CreditNoteCreate.reason as a plain {"type":"string"} with no enum, so a client cannot discover the permitted set from the spec, but the DB enforces CHECK ck_creditnotes_reason IN ('BILLING_ERROR','CUSTOMER_DISPUTE','GOODS_NOT_DELIVERED','OTHER'). The endpoint already has machinery to turn exactly this into a client error (`try: await db.commit() except DBAPIError: raise _as_client_error(...)`), but the constraint fires earlier during a query-invoked autoflush at the _build_line_item_rows db.get() â€” outside that try block â€” so it escapes as a 500. PUT /api/v1/credit-notes/{credit_note_id} fails identically (autoflush at the CreditNoteLineItem select on line 231).
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/credit_notes.py:187 (create) and :231/:234 (update) â€” the DBAPIError guard wraps only db.commit(), but autoflush emits the INSERT/UPDATE at the preceding SELECT/db.get(), so the constraint violation is raised outside it. Constraint defined at alembic/versions/0005_finance.py:636

Every sibling field in the same row is a resolved display value (customer name, formatted amount, date), so a dashboard rendering this row shows a UUID where "Cheque"/"NEFT" belongs. what_is_wrong: project_id is an advertised field of the InvoiceCreate body that PUT accepts and then silently discards. A client clearing or changing the project gets a 200 and an unchanged value, with no error and nothing in the response indicating the field was ignored. The code comment says this is deliberate ("locked after creation, just silent rather than a 422"), so this is a contract/UX defect rather than an accidental one â€” but as it stands the only two ways a caller can learn the field is immutable are reading the source or diffing the response. The sibling immutable field, customer_id, does raise a 422; project_id does not.
